name: Elderly Affairs Division, City and County of Honolulu
organization: Elderly Affairs Division, City and County of Honolulu
description: The Area Agency on Aging for this county: information and assistance, home-delivered and congregate meals, in-home services, transportation, caregiver support and senior legal assistance.
next_step: Call and describe what is hard right now. Ask for information and assistance. You can also call the statewide Aging and Disability Resource Center line, 808-643-2372. Military service is not required.
constraints: Many services focus on people age 60 and older and adults with disabilities; eligibility and waitlists vary by program.
The Aging and Disability Resource Center for O‘ahu.

source_evidence.title: Hawaii Executive Office on Aging: Aging Network
source_evidence.scope: The four Area Agencies on Aging and their phones (Hawai‘i County’s Kona line included); read in full. The Moloka‘i and Lāna‘i lines for the Maui County Office on Aging come from the Kaua‘i Agency on Elderly Affairs’ contact page (https://www.kauai.gov/Government/Departments-Agencies/Agency-on-Elderly-Affairs/Contact-Information-Links; search excerpt). Kalawao County, on Moloka‘i, is shown with the Maui County Office on Aging.

name: Hawai‘i Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
description: The regional long-term care ombudsman for this county: advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and residential care facilities.
next_step: Call the regional ombudsman program. Give the facility name and county. For immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing or enforcement agency.

source_evidence.title: Hawaii Executive Office on Aging
source_evidence.scope: For a problem, complaint or question about a long-term care facility, contact the LTC Ombudsman at 586-7268 (O‘ahu); search excerpt. The program is statewide, so every county shows it.
